answer: One summit meadow plot per identity locks an 85-credit bond and files an opal claim: area and weight. An auditor recomputes opal yield from area with the public opal-density table and summit thaw record, allowing 5% error. Shortfall, reuse, or a mismatched thaw date burns the bond. Under one key the fee is 41+8(k-1) for identity k, so the 1,000th pays 8,033 and 1,000 fakes pay 4,037,000 plus 85,000 in bonds. A rented-meadow ring fails: rented stones carry the owner's claim, mismatching the renter's area and burning both bonds. An honest claimant pays 41 once and recovers it after one epoch.
